query: Which  French ace pilot and adventurer fly L'Oiseau Blanc

pipeline_result.response: The French ace pilot and adventurer who flew "L'Oiseau Blanc" (White Bird) is Charles de Gaulle. He was born on March 23, 1912, in Saint-Malo, France, and passed away on October 12, 1990. De Gaulle was a renowned aviator and pilot of the Étoile du Sud aircraft, which he flew extensively during World War II. His flight took him to various locations around Europe, including the skies over the French Riviera, where he claimed the title "L'Oiseau Blanc" (White Bird).
